title: Contact Us
html:
Contact Us

Tell us what you need and we will come back with a tailored quotation. We work with importers, distributors, hospitality groups, promotional agencies and brand owners on custom compact and folding umbrellas. The more detail you share at this stage, the more accurate our first reply will be.

Send us your enquiry

Use the form below for new projects, repeat orders, sampling requests and specification questions. Fields marked with an asterisk are required. An estimated quantity is enough at this stage — you do not need a final purchase order yet.

What to include

  • Target product or category, and whether the design is yours or ours.
  • Estimated quantity per design, plus your target market or destination country.
  • Artwork files, Pantone references or a mood board, if available.
  • Your required delivery window and any inspection or compliance requirements.

Direct contact

  • Email: sales@fantasticumbrella.com
  • Phone / WhatsApp: +86 137 2520 9358
  • Address: Guangzhou, Guangdong, China
  • Business hours: Monday to Friday, 09:00-18:00 (GMT+8)
  • Response time: We reply to every enquiry within 24 working hours.

Why work with us

  • In-house digital printing with a dedicated team of around 15 in Guangzhou.
  • Partner factories of 300–400 workers for bulk production.
  • BSCI, SEDEX and ISO 9001 certified supply chain.
  • Every order is made to order and produced against an approved sample.

What happens next

  1. We confirm your requirements and send a quotation with MOQ, lead time and packing data.
  2. We prepare a sample for your written approval in 7–15 days.
  3. Production starts after sample sign-off; pre-shipment inspection runs before dispatch.

title: OEM & ODM Services
html:
We are a Guangzhou-based supplier of custom compact and folding umbrellas, built on in-house digital printing. Our own team of around 15 handles design, printing, sampling and export coordination, while partner factories of 300–400 workers handle bulk assembly. This structure keeps small runs flexible and bulk orders consistent.

What we make

  • Compact and folding rain umbrellas, including three-fold, five-fold and ultra-compact styles.
  • Straight, golf, children's and promotional umbrellas, with custom handles, frames and fabrics.
  • All-over digital printing, Pantone matching and private-label packaging.
  • A small selection of beach umbrellas and parasols for resort and promotional programmes.

Beach chairs, cabanas, sun shelters, gazebos and patio shade structures are handled by our GreenMark sister site.

Our capability matrix

Capability What we do Where
Digital printing All-over print, pattern placement, Pantone matching, small-batch runs In-house
Cutting & sewing Panel cutting, stitching, binding and finishing Partner workshops
Frame & hardware Shaft, ribs, handle and size options to your specification Partner workshops
Sampling Prototype, printed strike-off and pre-production sample In-house + workshop
Quality control Incoming, in-line and pre-shipment inspection to AQL 2.5 In-house + third party
Packaging & labelling Polybag, hangtag, barcode, custom carton and shipping mark Partner workshops

Custom Manufacturing

Send us your specification and we build to it — size, fabric, frame, print, packaging and carton mark. We confirm every parameter in writing before sampling, so the approved sample and the bulk order match. If a requested component is not available, we propose an alternative and explain the impact on commercial terms and lead time before you commit.

Private Label

We apply your brand across the product and the pack: woven or printed labels, hangtags, logo print, barcodes and custom cartons. Artwork is kept confidential and is never reused for other buyers. We can also follow your packaging specification, including carton dimensions and drop-test requirements.

OEM vs ODM

  • OEM: You supply the design, artwork and specification; we produce to your documents. Best when you already have a developed product.
  • ODM: You choose one of our existing umbrella or outdoor shapes and adapt the print, colour, trim and packaging. Best when you want a faster route to market.
  • Both routes include a pre-production sample for written approval before bulk production starts.

Sampling

  1. Share artwork (AI / PDF), Pantone references, size and target quantity.
  2. We confirm the specification and quote the sample cost and timeline.
  3. We produce a printed strike-off or full prototype in 7–15 days.
  4. You review and comment; we revise where needed.
  5. The approved sample becomes the reference for production and inspection.

Sample fees are quoted before any work starts and are deductible from the bulk order.

Quality Control

Every bulk order follows incoming material checks, a first-article approval, in-line checks and a pre-shipment inspection to AQL 2.5. We check print registration, colour consistency, dimensions, stitching and hardware function against the approved sample. Third-party inspection by SGS, BV or your own inspector is welcomed and supported. See Quality & Claims for our inspection and claim procedure.

MOQ & Capacity

MOQ starts at 300 pcs per design. Quantity tiers at 300 / 500 / 1,000+ pcs are quoted separately, and mixed designs in one order can be discussed when they share the same frame and fabric. Partner factories of 300–400 workers give us room for both trial runs and repeat seasonal volumes.

Trade Terms & Logistics

Standard terms are FOB Guangzhou / Shenzhen, with EXW and CIF available on request. Samples travel by express courier and bulk orders by sea or air freight. See Shipping & Delivery for transit times, packing data and destination charges; we prepare the commercial invoice, packing list and shipping documents for every order.

Certifications

Our supply chain is audited to BSCI and SEDEX, with ISO 9001 quality management. Copies of current certificates and audit summaries can be shared during supplier onboarding.

What happens next

  1. Share your brief. Specification, artwork, target quantity, destination and any compliance requirements.
  2. We confirm in writing. A specification sheet, quantity tier, sample cost and lead time before any work starts.
  3. Sample, production, inspection. The approved sample becomes the reference for production and pre-shipment inspection.

Request a Quote

Tell us what you are planning and we will recommend the right route — OEM or ODM — together with the appropriate quantity tier and sampling plan. Send your enquiry through the Contact page and we will reply with a full specification sheet and quotation.

Request a Quote

Common questions? See our B2B FAQ, or read Shipping & Delivery and Quality & Claims before you write.

MOQ, lead times and inspection standards are indicative and are confirmed in writing with your quotation and specification sheet.

title: B2B FAQ
html:
B2B FAQ

These are the questions we receive most often from importers, distributors and brand owners before a first order. The figures below are planning references and are confirmed in your quotation. If your question is not here, send it through the Contact page.

Ordering & MOQ

Q1. What is your MOQ?

MOQ starts at 300 pcs per design and is confirmed in the quotation based on the frame, fabric and printing method. Quantity tiers at 300 / 500 / 1,000+ pcs are quoted separately.

Q2. Can we order below the MOQ?

For a first trial we can often combine a smaller run with a shared fabric and frame configuration. Tell us your target quantity and we will confirm what is feasible before sampling, rather than after.

Q3. Can I mix designs or products in one order?

Mixed designs are possible when they share the same base specification, because printing and assembly are set up once. Mixed product categories in one shipment are also possible and are listed separately on the packing list.

Customisation & Sampling

Q4. What is the difference between OEM and ODM?

With OEM you supply the design and specification and we produce to your documents. With ODM you choose one of our existing shapes and adapt the print, colour, trim and packaging. Both routes include an approved pre-production sample.

Q5. How does the customisation process work?

It runs: enquiry → specification and quotation → sampling → written sample approval → production → pre-shipment inspection → shipment. Nothing enters production before the specification and sample are signed off.

Q6. What artwork files do you need?

Vector files in AI or PDF are preferred, with Pantone references and an indication of print placement. Minimum resolution and accepted file sizes are confirmed with your quotation. We return a digital layout for approval before printing the strike-off, so changes are caught early.

Q7. How long does sampling take, and is there a sample fee?

A printed strike-off or prototype takes 7–15 days. Sample fees and express freight are quoted before work starts and are deductible from the bulk order.

Commercial Terms & Delivery

Q8. What are your payment terms?

Standard terms are T/T with a 30% deposit and the balance before shipment or against a copy of the bill of lading. Sample fees can be settled by PayPal or T/T. Quotations are valid for 30 days and state the currency, Incoterm and validity date.

Q9. How long is production and delivery?

Bulk production takes 25–35 days after sample approval and deposit. Transit is typically 25–35 days by sea and 7–12 days by air; samples go by express in 3–7 days. We flag Chinese New Year and peak-season risks at quotation stage.

Q10. Which Incoterms do you offer?

FOB Guangzhou / Shenzhen is standard, with EXW and CIF available on request. Import duties, taxes and destination charges are for the buyer’s account under FOB and CIF. See Shipping & Delivery for the full breakdown.

Quality, Compliance & After-Sales

Q11. What certifications and audits do you have?

Our supply chain is audited to BSCI and SEDEX, with ISO 9001 quality management. Copies of current certificates and audit summaries can be shared during supplier onboarding.

Q12. How do you handle inspection and claims?

Pre-shipment inspection follows AQL 2.5 and third-party inspectors are welcome. Claims should be raised within 30 days of arrival with photos, carton numbers and the packing list; remedies are a replacement or a credit note. Full steps are on the Quality & Claims page.

Request a Quote

Ready to discuss a project? Send your specification, estimated quantity and target market through the Contact page and we will reply with a quotation and a sampling plan.

title: Shipping & Delivery
html:
Shipping & Delivery

All orders are made to order and shipped from Guangdong, China. We confirm the shipping method, transit time and packing data in writing before production starts, so you can plan your landing schedule. The figures below are planning references and are confirmed per order.

Samples

  • Sent by DHL / FedEx express, typically 3–7 working days door to door.
  • Tracking is shared as soon as the parcel is collected.
  • Sample freight is quoted separately and is deductible from the bulk order.
  • For printed strike-offs, a scanned or photographed approval can be arranged first to save a round of shipping.

Bulk Orders — Sea Freight

  • Port-to-port transit is typically 25–35 days, depending on destination and sailing schedule.
  • FCL and LCL are both available; we recommend the option based on volume and carton dimensions.
  • Standard loading port: Guangzhou / Shenzhen. Booking is confirmed before ex-works dispatch.
  • Original documents or telex release are arranged according to your requirement and payment status.

Bulk Orders — Air Freight

  • Door-to-airport transit is typically 7–12 days including handling.
  • Suitable for urgent launches, trade show samples and seasonal top-ups.
  • Chargeable weight is calculated from carton dimensions; we provide packing data before booking.

Incoterms We Work With

  • EXW — You arrange collection from our workshop and handle all export and onward transport.
  • FOB Guangzhou / Shenzhen — We handle export clearance and loading on board; you nominate the carrier and manage main carriage.
  • CIF — We arrange main carriage and marine insurance to your destination port; you handle import clearance and onward delivery.
  • Other terms can be discussed for specific projects. We state the applicable Incoterm on every quotation and commercial invoice.

Lead Time Breakdown

Stage Planning reference
Sampling & approval 7–15 days
Bulk production 25–35 days after sample approval and deposit
Inspection & booking 3–5 days
Sea / air transit 25–35 days / 7–12 days

Peak periods such as Chinese New Year and trade show season can extend production and booking windows. We flag any risk at quotation stage rather than after production starts.

Packaging & Loading

  • Each unit is individually packed; cartons are sized to your specification or our standard export carton.
  • Units per carton, carton dimensions, gross / net weight and total CBM are provided with the quotation and packing list.
  • 20GP / 40HQ loading quantities can be calculated once the carton specification is confirmed.
  • Shipping marks, barcodes and carton labels follow your artwork, or our standard neutral mark.

Shipping Documents

  • Commercial invoice and packing list.
  • Bill of lading or air waybill.
  • Certificate of origin, where required.
  • Copies of BSCI / SEDEX / ISO 9001 certificates and test reports, where required for your market.

Destination Charges

Under FOB and CIF terms, import duties, taxes, customs clearance fees, port charges and inland delivery at destination are for the buyer’s account. Confirm the applicable HS code and any market-specific requirements with your broker before placing the order. We can share product composition and material details to support classification.

Request a Quote

Tell us your destination port, required delivery window and expected volume. We will confirm the shipping method, Incoterm, packing data and a realistic timeline in the quotation.

title: Quality & Claims
html:
Quality & Claims

Quality is managed against the approved pre-production sample, not against a generic catalogue description. We document the specification, inspection standard and remedy terms before production starts, so both sides know what will be checked and what happens if something goes wrong.

Our QC Process

  1. Incoming materials — Fabric, frame components, printing substrates and packaging are checked against the confirmed specification.
  2. First-article approval — The first unit off the line is compared with the approved sample and signed off internally.
  3. In-line inspection — Print registration, colour, stitching and assembly are checked during production, not only at the end.
  4. Pre-shipment inspection — A random sample is inspected to AQL 2.5 before cartons are sealed.

Inspection Standards

  • AQL 2.5 for major and minor defects, applied to a random sample.
  • Dimensional tolerance, colour deviation and print placement are defined in the specification sheet.
  • Function checks cover opening / closing, tilt mechanism, ribs, pole and hardware.
  • If your company uses a different AQL or a custom checklist, send it with the enquiry and we will quote against it.

Third-Party Inspection

We welcome inspections by SGS, BV or your own nominated inspector before shipment. We share the production schedule and packing list in advance so the inspection can be booked without delaying the vessel. Inspection findings are recorded and resolved before dispatch.

Before You File a Claim

  • Raise any claim within 30 days of arrival at your destination port.
  • Keep the original cartons, shipping marks and packing list until the claim is closed.
  • Record the issue with photos or video, including the carton mark and the defect.
  • Note the purchase order number, carton numbers and the quantity affected.

Claim Process

  1. Send the evidence and a short description to sales@fantasticumbrella.com.
  2. We acknowledge receipt within 24 working hours and register the claim.
  3. We review the evidence against the approved sample, inspection record and production batch.
  4. We confirm the finding and propose a remedy in writing, normally within 5 working days.
  5. The agreed remedy is applied to your next shipment or settled separately.

Remedies

  • Replacement of the affected units in your next production shipment.
  • A credit note offset against a future order.
  • Other settlements by mutual agreement, documented in writing.
  • We do not apply consumer-style returns handling; every claim is resolved against the original order specification.

Responsibility

We take responsibility for We cannot take responsibility for
Manufacturing defects against the approved sample Damage during transit, loading, unloading or storage after transfer of risk
Wrong artwork, colour or print placement caused in production Errors in artwork or specifications supplied by the buyer and approved in writing
Quantity shortage against the packing list Normal wear, misuse, or alterations made after delivery
Packaging that fails the agreed carton specification Delays or charges caused by destination customs or the buyer’s broker

Responsibility is determined from the inspection record, packing list and arrival documentation.

Documents Needed for a Claim

  • Purchase order number and commercial invoice reference.
  • Bill of lading or air waybill and the packing list.
  • Photos / video of the defect and of the outer carton with the shipping mark.
  • Count of affected units and their carton numbers.
  • The approved sample or specification sheet reference, where relevant.

Request a Quote / Contact

Questions about inspection standards, documentation or a specific claim can be sent to sales@fantasticumbrella.com. We reply within 24 working hours.
